versions.provenance: 8th edition (and FIGO where applicable) cervix staging, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
8th edition staging of cervical carcinoma covers carcinomas of the cervix uteri and is aligned with the FIGO 2018 revision, so the T categories correspond directly to FIGO stages (shown in each label). The common histologies are squamous cell carcinoma, adenocarcinoma, and adenosquamous carcinoma; extension to the uterine corpus is disregarded for the primary tumour category.

What is notable in 8th edition is that it follows FIGO 2018, which introduced size-based subdivisions of stage IB (IB1 tumour < 2 cm, IB2 2 to < 4 cm, IB3 >= 4 cm), removed horizontal tumour extent from the definition of stage IA, and added stage IIIC for lymph node metastasis (IIIC1 pelvic nodes, IIIC2 para-aortic nodes). Imaging and pathologic findings may be used to assign stage. A key nuance is that para-aortic nodes are regional (not distant) disease, and depth of stromal invasion, lymphovascular space invasion, and node status are the main prognostic drivers.

t.label: T1 (FIGO I): Carcinoma confined to the cervix uteri; extension to the uterine corpus is disregarded
T1a (FIGO IA): Invasive carcinoma diagnosed only by microscopy, with a maximum depth of stromal invasion < 5 mm
T1a1 (FIGO IA1): Measured stromal invasion < 3 mm in depth
T1a2 (FIGO IA2): Measured stromal invasion >= 3 mm and < 5 mm in depth
T1b (FIGO IB): Invasive carcinoma with measured deepest invasion >= 5 mm (beyond T1a), lesion limited to the cervix uteri
T1b1 (FIGO IB1): Invasion >= 5 mm in depth and tumor < 2 cm in greatest dimension
T1b2 (FIGO IB2): Tumor >= 2 cm and < 4 cm in greatest dimension
T1b3 (FIGO IB3): Tumor >= 4 cm in greatest dimension
T2 (FIGO II): Carcinoma invades beyond the uterus but not onto the pelvic wall or the lower third of the vagina
T2a (FIGO IIA): Involvement limited to the upper two-thirds of the vagina, without parametrial invasion
T2a1 (FIGO IIA1): Tumor < 4 cm in greatest dimension
T2a2 (FIGO IIA2): Tumor >= 4 cm in greatest dimension
T2b (FIGO IIB): Parametrial invasion, but not extending to the pelvic wall
T3 (FIGO III): Tumor involves the lower third of the vagina and/or extends to the pelvic wall and/or causes hydronephrosis or a nonfunctioning kidney
T3a (FIGO IIIA): Tumor involves the lower third of the vagina, with no extension to the pelvic wall
T3b (FIGO IIIB): Extension to the pelvic wall and/or hydronephrosis or a nonfunctioning kidney (unless known to be due to another cause)
T4 (FIGO IVA): Tumor invades the mucosa of the bladder or rectum and/or extends beyond the true pelvis (bullous edema alone does not qualify as T4; must be biopsy proven)

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Isolated tumor cells in regional lymph node(s) no larger than 0.2 mm
N1 (FIGO IIIC): Regional lymph node metastasis. FIGO subdivides by location: pelvic nodes only = IIIC1; para-aortic nodes = IIIC2 (para-aortic nodes are regional for cervix)

m.label: M1 (FIGO IVB): Distant metastasis, including peritoneal spread; involvement of supraclavicular, mediastinal, or distant lymph nodes; and metastasis to lung, liver, or bone

stageGroups.basis: Microscopic invasion >= 3 to < 5 mm deep, node-negative.
Invasion >= 5 mm deep, tumor < 2 cm, node-negative.
Tumor >= 2 to < 4 cm, confined to cervix, node-negative.
Tumor >= 4 cm, confined to cervix, node-negative.
Upper two-thirds vaginal involvement, tumor < 4 cm, no parametrial invasion, node-negative.
Upper two-thirds vaginal involvement, tumor >= 4 cm, no parametrial invasion, node-negative.
Parametrial invasion without pelvic wall extension, node-negative.
Lower-third vaginal involvement without pelvic wall extension, node-negative.
Pelvic wall extension and/or hydronephrosis, node-negative.
Pelvic lymph node metastasis only, irrespective of tumor size/extent.
Para-aortic lymph node metastasis, irrespective of tumor size/extent.
Invasion of bladder/rectal mucosa or spread beyond the true pelvis.

versions.regionalNodes: Regional lymph nodes include the paracervical, parametrial, hypogastric (internal iliac and obturator), external iliac, common iliac, presacral, and para-aortic nodes. Para-aortic nodal metastasis is regional (N1 / FIGO IIIC2), not distant.
versions.histologicGrade: GX (grade not assessable), G1 (well differentiated), G2 (moderately differentiated), G3 (poorly differentiated or undifferentiated).
versions.histopathologicTypes: Squamous cell carcinoma (most common), adenocarcinoma, adenosquamous carcinoma, and less common types including neuroendocrine (small cell and large cell) carcinoma, glassy cell carcinoma, and clear cell carcinoma.
prognosticFactors: FIGO stage and tumor size (greatest dimension)
Regional lymph node status (pelvic vs para-aortic)
Parametrial involvement and surgical margin status
Histologic type (neuroendocrine and adenosquamous carry a worse prognosis) and grade
